scope: Server-owned CityRef integration for LiteAPI sandbox and Duffel test; no new actual network, LLM, DB or Native changes.

interfaces.list_countries: list_countries()->list[{country_iso2,name}], one sandbox GET /v3.0/data/countries, strict code/name response fields, bounded<=300.
interfaces.hotel_lookup: resolve_hotels(legacy_city_string OR {city?:exact_name,place_ref:server_snapshot},limit<=10). Legacy string behavior unchanged; a ref lookup performs at most one HTTP request.
interfaces.air_lookup: resolve_air_place({place_ref:server_snapshot})->status RESOLVED|AMBIGUOUS|NO_MATCH|UNVERIFIED, place_id/country/refSHA, optional confirmed IATA/provider ID, identity and availability flags.
interfaces.private_requests: Only internal server orchestration injects place_ref for hotel requests and place_refs={origin?,destination?} for a single flight leg; these are never supplier payload fields.

verified_controlled_behavior: HYBRID request capabilities append structurally valid owned ref names; DEMO registry remains the original seven synthetic cities.

Dynamic hotel lookup requires exact normalized city, exact country and finite coordinates within a 50km consistency radius from the selected geographic point. Missing or contradictory metadata is blocked; no nearest-town substitution.
Legacy aliases are accepted only when their fixed seed country matches the selected snapshot country; a Moscow/US ref never inherits the Moscow/RU mapping.
Hotel rates require fresh same-gateway identity evidence for all requested IDs. Conflicting included rate metadata and unrequested IDs are not promoted to the selected geography.
A pinned dynamic hotel must be among the verified lookup IDs; another result is never silently substituted.

Air resolution prefers an unambiguous exact metro city. Spatial evidence comes from city coordinates, an explicit linked airport within the same country/radius, or an already verified matching provider binding. Unknown or ambiguous associations remain blockers.
No airport timezone is copied into city state. No candidate airport is chosen by nearest distance.
Dynamic flight requests require fresh matched IATA/ref evidence and a response confirming the requested route/date; a 200 response with missing slices is not enough.
Orchestration resolves dynamic endpoint IDs explicitly under the shared tool budget, memoizes by physical ref ID plus snapshot SHA, and retains actual components when another component fails.

Any trip containing dynamic refs disables synthetic fallback for the whole route. DEMO mode with refs returns structured incomplete output; existing unreferenced seven-city behavior remains unchanged.

verification.initial_failure_attribution: Three initial orchestration fixture failures used inherited Oct25 offers against declared Oct27 test clock. The existing stale-source guard correctly rejected them. Fixture timestamps were corrected; assertions were not weakened.

two_homonym_ref_case.source_facts: declared controlled fixture, not actual supplier evidence

limits: 50km is a consistency guard, not a municipal boundary, best nearby choice, supplier availability guarantee or approved product coverage cap.
Physical identity, hotel ID metadata, fare eligibility and supplier inventory availability remain separate facts.
Country-list field parsing is supported by official documentation, not a newly executed actual countries call.
No natural-language global model flow, actual world hotel/flight availability, booking, payment or successful whole-cart checkout is claimed.
Missing transfer integration keeps a global trip partial; no global synthetic catalogue or false READY result is created.
API/Store must authenticate client-supplied ref snapshots before internal private request injection; structural gateway DTO checks alone are not catalog provenance.
Ruff changed no LLMGateway code; existing orchestrator fault-boundary lint rules are not claimed as repository-wide lint closure.
